stem: Two plants receive the same nutrient solution but one develops symptoms where the root zone is persistently wetter and less aerated. What does this pattern suggest?
choices: Root-zone physical conditions may be influencing nutrient uptake or root function, so solution composition alone may not explain the symptoms
The nutrient solution must contain different concentrations for each plant
The symptomatic plant necessarily has different genetics
rationale: Nutrient uptake depends on functioning roots. Spatial association with poor aeration supports evaluating root-zone condition before changing solution composition.
